props.title: Real Waves
props.videoLabel: Godot 4.7.2 · Forward+ · low camera · same shader
props.caption: PlaneMesh: vertices = (cuts + 2) × (cuts + 2)

B34.capture_spec: C25: scene water_scene.gd, W_BARE low camera, shader 05-vertex-waves (TIME): left an UNCUT plane, right cut 127 x 127; both 1080 x 1080 joined. Vertex counts are read from the mesh (facts1_classdb.gd: 4, 25, 4225, 16,641).
B34.visual_intent: Act title 'Real Waves'; two framed views of the same wave shader from just above the waterline: the uncut plane only tilts (straight edges), the cut plane rolls with real waves; pills '4 vertices' and '16,641 vertices'.
B34.motion_claim: The left plane tilts like a board; the right plane rolls like water.
B34.runner_up: manim: a dot grid counting up
B34.why: Two real planes with the same shader are the lesson; the count pills carry the numbers.

cues.label: phase: position minus speed times time
sine: a smooth wave between -1 and 1
x: height · y, z: slope along x and z

props.videoLabel: Godot 4.7.2 · Forward+ · low camera · live clock
props.caption: two waves, two directions, two lengths, added

B35.capture_spec: C26: scene water_scene.gd, W_BARE low camera, shader 05-vertex-waves cut 127, TIME from the capture start.
B35.visual_intent: Code card with the last six lines of wave() (the phase line, the sine line and the return line lit in turn); the real low view of the plane with a lumpy rolling surface.
B35.motion_claim: Two waves of different lengths roll through each other.
B35.why: The real rolling surface is the sum; the code beside it is the recipe.

cues.label: TIME: seconds on one clock shared by the whole game
vertex(): runs once for each vertex; places the corners

props.caption: one line moves 16,641 vertices; the card fills in between

B36.capture_spec: C27: scene water_scene.gd, shader 05-vertex-waves cut 127, iso camera, TIME from the capture start; floaters not following (still).
B36.visual_intent: Code card (the vertex function; the wave call then the add-to-y line lit); the real cove with rolling waves: the shoreline against the beach wobbles, the floaters stay at y 0.
B36.motion_claim: The water surface rolls and the shoreline wobbles.
B36.why: The real rolling shoreline is the effect of the one line.

cues.label: normal: a direction at right angles to a surface

props.videoLabel: Godot 4.7.2 · Forward+ · normal line added at 55 %
props.caption: the glare: one flat oval, then glints on the crests

B37.capture_spec: C28: scene water_scene.gd, W_FOLLOW, shader 05c-no-normal-update (NORMAL line removed) swapped at 55 % for 05b-synced-clock; ripples and foam turned down (ripple_strength 0, edge_width 0.01) so the glare is the only light effect.
B37.visual_intent: Code card (the vertex function, NORMAL line lit); the real cove with rolling waves: first the sun's glare is one flat oval whatever the waves do, then after 55 % it breaks into glints along the crests; pills 'old normal' and 'new normal'.
B37.motion_claim: The one flat glare shatters into crest glints when the normal line arrives.
B37.runner_up: manim: normals drawn on a wave
B37.why: A real before and after of the same waves shows the light not knowing; a drawing of normals would explain the maths only.

props.videoLabel: Godot 4.7.2 · Forward+ · low camera · script clock
props.caption: near edge, lowest to highest row: up to 95 rows (flat plane: 0)

B38.capture_spec: C29: scene water_scene.gd, W_BARE low camera, shader 05b-synced-clock cut 127, wave_clock from the script (W_FOLLOW); the 95-row figure is the maximum over the recorded clip (40 to 96 rows, mean 78, logs/edge-spread.txt) and the still (95).
B38.visual_intent: The framed window shows the plane from just above the waterline: the near edge is a rolling line; the pill 'up to 95' sits below it.
B38.motion_claim: The near edge of the water rolls up and down.
B38.runner_up: manim: a straight line and a wavy line
B38.why: The same camera as the flat plane two beats ago, now with an edge that bends: the contrast is real and measured.

cues.label: the same two waves as the shader, in GDScript

props.caption: a script sets each floater's height from the same function

B39.capture_spec: C30: scene water_scene.gd, W_FOLLOW: water_driver.gd drives wave_clock and sets the buoy and the crate to WaveMath.height each frame; shader 05b, iso camera.
B39.visual_intent: Code card with the eight GDScript lines of the height function (first line lit); the real cove: the teal buoy and the cream crate rise and fall exactly with the waves.
B39.motion_claim: The buoy and the crate ride the crests and troughs.
B39.runner_up: manim: a node and the invisible surface
B39.why: Floaters riding the real waves are the point; the code is the other half.

B40.visual_intent: Two horizontal time lines labelled 'shader time' and 'script clock' with tick marks; the script's line starts later: a bracket between the two starts is labelled with the three measured gaps '0.32 s', '0.28 s', '0.31 s' (three of the six logged real-time runs, which ranged 0.28 to 0.32 s); then a box labelled 'wave_clock' (a uniform) receives an arrow from the script line, and the shader line is redrawn lined up with it; the final state shows both lines aligned with 'one number' between them.
B40.motion_claim: The script line slides to the right to show the gap, three gap labels appear one per run, then an arrow into the uniform box pulls the two lines into alignment.
B40.why: Two clocks and a gap between them is a timeline diagram; the three measured offsets make it real.

props.videoLabel: Godot 4.7.2 · Forward+ · script clock · scripted sweeps
props.caption: GPU and script heights agree to 3 mm on waves 192 mm tall

B41.capture_spec: C31: scene water_scene.gd, W_FOLLOW, shader 05b: the driver's wave_height, wave_length and wave_speed are swept one after another between 56 % and 95 % of the beat; the 3 mm agreement is E9 (evidence/planning-checks).
B41.visual_intent: Code card (the driver's set_clock lines; the three uniform writes lit one by one); the real cove: the waves grow taller, then longer, then faster, with the floaters still riding them; pills 'within 3 mm', 'height', 'length', 'speed'.
B41.motion_claim: Height, length and speed are swept in turn and the buoy keeps riding.
B41.why: Three sweeps on the real water show what each dial changes.
